The dispatcher indexes the five self-relative words of Enemy_Stage10BeetleStateOffsets.
Five self-relative words naming the init, initial delay, roam, bounce and exit states.

Entity_UpdateHandlerTable installs this entry. It clears the shake request in $52, runs the state machine, and only then raises PlaneAShakeLevel to the requested value, halving it for plane B, so individual states request shake intensity rather than setting it.

Before dispatching, the routine forces state $1E once BossHealth reaches zero with no colour effect already active, pauses the stage timer, and otherwise refreshes the palette and caches the camera-relative X in $5E.
Normal and forced-defeat paths converge here for palette update, position derivation, and state dispatch.
The dispatcher indexes the seventeen word offsets of Boss_JetsripperStates, which are measured from Boss_JetsripperInitState rather than being absolute addresses.
Boss_JetsripperStateDispatch indexes these seventeen relative handler offsets with object state field 4.
State 0 advances by two, anchors the chain head to the boss itself, and tail-calls Object_ClearEntityRecordsExceptTwoTypes sparing type $E4.
State 2 selects state $10 and then initializes eighteen contiguous segment records, alternating the collision byte between $50 and $10 on odd indices and spacing the per-segment field $48 by six.
This eighteen-iteration loop initializes one contiguous $60-byte Jetsripper segment object.
Both collision variants converge here to install the shared hitbox, health and contact fields before the loop advances to the next $60-byte record.
State $10 oscillates until the cached camera-relative X passes $810, then advances and seeds the angle timer with $40.
State entry $12 is a single branch into Boss_JetsripperAlignToCenter, which state entry 4 also names directly; the name now says which state it re-enters.
State $14 spends the countdown in $5C and, on expiry, plays SFX $48, requests shake level 8, and starts boss message 3 before continuing into the shared movement update.
State $16 waits for MessageSequenceState to clear, then returns to state 6, rearms the $5C countdown, clears the colour-effect flags, and widens the camera's left bound by $A0.
State 8 steps the angle up by eight units per frame and leaves only when the countdown in $4C has expired and the angle lands exactly on $70.
Active rotation and completed transition paths converge here to store the normalized body angle.
Several early states converge here to calculate, link, render, and vertically clamp all segments.
In-range and clamped body Y paths share this segment-display return.

State $A oscillates while draining BossCombatCounter; it takes the dive state at angle zero past X $710, or on a random bit above counter $12 takes the swing state, and enters the rotate state when the counter runs out.
When the primary idle-to-align condition fails, this block tests timer, random bit, angle, and direction for the alternate attack transition.
The patrol timeout sets direction field $4C to one, which selects angle subtraction in the oscillation helper.
The idle timeout clears direction field $4C, which selects angle addition in the oscillation helper.
Both timeout directions converge here to select state 4 and initialize rotation and state timers.
State $C is the mirror of the rotate state: it steps the angle down by eight and leaves when the angle lands exactly on $90.
Incomplete and completed alignment paths converge here to store the normalized angle before rendering.
State $E mirrors the idle state with the opposite angle direction, using the $100 angle and the X $870 threshold instead.
When the primary patrol-to-rotate condition fails, this block tests timer, random bit, angle, and direction for the alternate transition.
The shared helper requests shake level 1, converges the radius, and swings the angle by eight units in the direction held in $4C, reversing whenever the $4E timer expires and reloading it with $18.
A nonzero direction field selects the angle-subtraction half of the oscillation cycle.
Both completed half-cycles converge here to reload the $18-frame direction timer.
Both swing directions converge here to normalize the angle into the $1F8 range, store it, and add the scaled sine velocity to the vertical accumulator at $130.
State 4 requests shake level 2 and biases the angle by $10 or $30 depending on the direction flag while converging the radius.
Both direction variants converge here to mask the candidate angle to sixteen-step increments.
Completed and incomplete alignment paths converge here to store the angle and update the segment chain.
State 6 refills BossCombatCounter by two per frame and picks a randomized angle step between $18 and $27, reversing direction at the $100 and $180 angle limits.
Direction zero selects this angle-increment and timer-decrement path.
Reaching the increasing-angle limit or expiring its timer sets direction field $4C to one.
Direction one selects this angle-decrement and timer-decrement path.
Reaching the decreasing-angle limit or expiring its timer clears the direction field.
Both direction switches reload field $4E with the randomized angle-cycle duration.
All angle-cycle paths converge here to normalize and store the new angle before attack-state checks.
A segment X position below $7C0 selects state $0C, the alignment state, after firing.
Movement, alignment, and attack paths converge here to update and render the linked segment chain.
The movement state ends by alternating between the two body mappings on bit 2 of the frame counter and clearing the vertical flip.
Boss_JetsripperSelectSprite indexes these two body mappings with the shared animation phase bit.
State $18 drains BossCombatCounter, keeps the sine velocity accumulating, and rotates until the angle reaches $180 before the dive proper begins.
When the dive angle is not yet $180, this block selects increment or decrement according to the direction field.
A nonzero direction field selects angle subtraction and reloads the angle timer.
Both dive-preparation rotation directions converge here to normalize and store the angle.
State $1A clears the horizontal velocity and rotates the chain in $20-unit steps, reversing at the $80 angle, and refills the angle history when the dive relaunches.
Direction zero advances both the secondary rotation and main angle during the dive windup.
Both dive rotation directions converge here to store the main and secondary angles and expand the chain radius.
The two player-side-dependent launch velocities converge at this post-launch return.
Before maximum radius, this path recalculates, links, and renders the dive-windup segment chain.
State $1C swings the shared angle offset $5A and the per-segment step $BE together, reversing between the $1C and $FFE4 limits, and seeds a gradient angle history at each reversal.
Direction zero applies the opposite signed changes to the swing angles and curvature accumulator.
Both swing directions converge here to normalize and store angles before updating the segment buffer.
Clamped and unclamped radius paths converge here to apply vertical acceleration and test landing.
The alternate player-side result selects state $0C and the opposite angle-gradient direction.
The helper recomputes the per-segment radii, drives all seventeen segments from the angle history, resets both chain anchors to the boss, and refreshes every segment sprite.
State $1E arms a $C0-frame fade, spawns one type-$EC head effect when a slot is free, and converts the seventeen segment records into type-$EC debris, giving the last one the tail frame table.
Optional primary effect creation and allocation failure converge here before converting the remaining segment slots to type $EC effects.
This seventeen-iteration loop configures one contiguous segment slot as a type-$EC death effect.
Death-effect initialization and an active fade timer share this state return.
State $20 randomizes the palette range each frame until the $C0-frame counter expires, then clears every entity record.
The helper converges chain radius $54 toward $C0 in steps of $A from either side, snapping to $C0 once the remaining distance falls inside the dead band.
Candidate radii crossing either tolerance threshold converge here to store the target radius $C0.
Current radii at or above $C0 take this decrement-toward-target path.
Candidate radii outside the snap tolerance are stored here unchanged.

The routine has no static caller and its absolute address does not occur in the ROM; it steps angle field $56 by eight units in the direction held by flag $4C, reverses at the $58 boundary, and pins the opposite limit at $1B0 until the object's Y coordinate $14 reaches $128.
A clear direction field branches here to increase the object's angle by eight units and test the lower reversal boundary.
Both angle directions and their boundary cases converge here to store the normalized angle.

The routine has no static caller and its absolute address does not occur in the ROM; it scans the current object plus seventeen contiguous $60-byte segment records for the largest fixed-point Y coordinate, publishes the winner in fields $48 and $4A, and clamps that object's Y to $144.
This seventeen-iteration scan compares the next contiguous segment's fixed-point Y coordinate against the current largest value.
Selected and rejected candidates converge here before advancing to the next $60-byte segment object.

Boss_JetsripperRotateState and Boss_JetsripperUpdateMovement call this narrower live variant, which considers only the five middle segments from the eighth through the twelfth entity record rather than the whole chain, then stores the visually lowest one in fields $48 and $4A and clamps its Y to $144.
This four-iteration Jetsripper scan compares each candidate's fixed-point Y coordinate and retains the largest value, which is visually lowest.
Selected and rejected Jetsripper candidates converge here before advancing to the next $60-byte object.

The routine refreshes the entire chain in three passes over consecutive $60-byte records: one head sprite from Boss_JetsripperHeadFrames, sixteen body sprites from Boss_JetsripperBodyDirectionFrames, and a trailing tail sprite for which it falls through into Boss_JetsripperUpdateEndSprite a second time.
Boss_JetsripperUpdateAllSprites calls the same four-direction routine once with the head frame table and then falls through to it with the tail frame table; its role is not head-only.
Both halves of the vertical-orientation test converge here to configure the other sprite flip bit.
All four-direction orientation quadrants converge here to quantize the angle and load a head or tail mapping pointer.

Each iteration adds the chain's shared angle offset $5A(a5) to the segment's own angle $56, derives the horizontal flip bit from the sum, and indexes the sixteen-entry body table; the caller's d7 supplies one pass per body segment.
Both flip outcomes converge here to round the angle to one of sixteen $20-unit sectors, load the matching mapping pointer into field $8, and advance to the next $60-byte segment record.
The live renderer supplies this four-entry mapping-pointer table for the head, and the death initializer attaches it to the first falling segment.
The live body renderer indexes these sixteen mapping pointers by angle; the death handler uses the same table to identify body segments.
The live renderer supplies this four-entry mapping-pointer table for the tail, and the death initializer attaches it to the final falling segment.

Boss_JetsripperInitBody and Boss_JetsripperDiveExecute reach this entry to write the caller's d0 into all seventy-two words of JetsripperAngleHistory, collapsing the chain onto a single angle in one frame.

Both Boss_JetsripperSwingAttack calls seed the same seventy-two-word history from boss angle $56, advancing each successive word by the caller's d1 step so the chain takes a curved pose without waiting for the history to fill.
This 72-iteration loop writes an angle and advances it by the caller-provided gradient for the next history-buffer word.
The routine never writes a Y-position field. It converts the controller's radius field $54 into seventeen per-segment $54 radius values consumed by the sine-based position routines.
Repeated subtraction of $11 derives the uniform radius tier and the remainder used for the leading segments.
This seventeen-iteration loop stores the derived radius tier into field $54 of each contiguous chain segment.
The remainder controls how many leading segment radius fields are decremented after the uniform assignment.
This is not a pure math helper: it reads the current boss object's angle, scales a sine-table value, and writes the result directly to horizontal velocity field $18(a5).
The routine returns in d2 a scaled sine value derived from Jetsripper angle field $176; it does not itself write a vertical-velocity field.

The routine has no static caller and its absolute address does not occur in the ROM; it accumulates the $4C and $4E deltas outward from the tenth entity record across nine segment pairs, then rebuilds seventeen segment positions from the sine table.
This symmetric nine-pair loop accumulates the two caller-supplied angle deltas into segment fields on both sides of the chain center.
This seventeen-iteration loop converts each segment's angle and radius into fixed-point positions relative to the preceding chain object.

The live per-frame update pushes the current boss angle onto the seventy-two-word history, then walks JetsripperAngleTapBase in eight-byte strides so each of the seventeen segments samples a progressively older angle and trails the head.
This 72-word loop inserts the current angle at the head of the history buffer while shifting each prior value forward.
This seventeen-iteration loop samples staggered history-buffer angles and derives one segment's angle and fixed-point position per iteration.

Boss_JetsripperUpdateState calls this every active frame; frame-counter bit 1 and a masked random gate select one of the three colour triples in Boss_JetsripperPaletteFrames before they are written over PaletteActiveColor61.

Entity_UpdateHandlerTable installs this handler directly, and its whole body clamps the object's Y coordinate $14 to the same $144 floor value that the segment scans enforce.
Already-in-range and clamped segment Y paths share this return.

Entity_UpdateHandlerTable installs this handler for detached segments: while field 4 is still clear it counts down delay $48, then sets field 4, launches the segment upward, shakes plane A and spawns a debris effect; later frames add constant gravity to $1C and spin the angle by $20, selecting a frame from whichever mapping table field $4C holds.
Non-body segments converge here to set their second flip bit from the current angle before selecting a four-direction frame.
The end-segment path quantizes its angle to four entries and loads the corresponding head or tail mapping pointer.
Segments carrying the sixteen-entry body table branch here to update the horizontal flip bit from their angle.
The body-segment path quantizes its angle to sixteen entries and loads the corresponding body mapping pointer.
An uninitialized death segment waits on field $48, then enables gravity, creates its launch effect, and starts its fall.
The active delay and failed effect-allocation paths share this return from the death-segment handler.
The block copies the selected fixed-point X and Y velocity components into fields $18 and $1C; the full word 'Velocity' follows the project naming contract.
Projectile allocation failure and successful velocity setup share this spawn-helper return.
Projectile positions outside the accepted camera-relative interval, or an inactive arena state, converge here to set the standard object deactivation bit.
This path consumes projectile flag bits $22.7 and $22.4, optionally creates a large pickup, and converts the projectile into a four-way burst.
Impact branches converge here to clear both velocity components and tail-call the shared four-projectile spawner.
Without an impact flag, this block selects the upper or lower vertical boundary test according to the signed Y acceleration component.
Crossing either vertical boundary restores horizontal velocity, negates both vertical parameters, and reloads the nine-frame trajectory interval.
A negative vertical parameter selects this comparison against the upper Y boundary $CC.
Between bounce resets, this block counts down field $58 and subtracts the stored X and Y increments from the active velocities.
The block only clears the projectile palette bits, merges the global palette selector, and returns; it is not a generic finalization routine.

Normal and externally forced encounter paths converge here for palette, camera-relative X, vertical acceleration, floor clamp, and flash-state updates.
Initialization bypasses and active updates converge here to dispatch field 4 through the twenty-entry SniperHoneyviper state table.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperDispatchState indexes these twenty relative offsets, whose destinations cover encounter initialization, combat, and defeat states.
The routine performs no proximity comparison. It advances SniperHoneyviper's state, installs the encounter background configuration, and removes object types other than the two supplied exceptions.
The complete routine consists of one RTS and has no known static reference; the name claims only its observed behavior.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperBeginEncounter stores this address in the global scrolling-background configuration pointer before later SniperHoneyviper states call Tilemap_QueueNextScrollingRow.

This state waits for Tilemap_QueueNextScrollingRow to report completion, advances encounter state, processes the terminated initial asset descriptors, and builds the shared sine/cosine displacement tables.

Boss_SniperHoneyviperQueueIndexedTileColumnsAfterAssets supplies this descriptor directly to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns.

The state configures SniperHoneyviper's raster and scroll globals, initializes the root and second embedded records, five descriptor-addressed auxiliaries, six consecutive chain parts, and a final table-driven object group.
This five-iteration loop initializes one object address and three sprite words from the auxiliary-part descriptor table.
This six-iteration loop initializes contiguous $60-byte SniperHoneyviper chain-part objects while stepping their sprite offset byte.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperInitializeEncounterEntities consumes this range as five records containing an object address and three sprite descriptor words.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperInitializeEncounterEntities assigns this three-word descriptor to the primary SniperHoneyviper object sprite fields.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperInitializeEncounterEntities assigns this three-word descriptor to the second embedded entity's sprite fields at offset $68.

After motion phase $16C falls below six, this state selects rotation state $E when BossCombatCounter is at least $13C and state zero otherwise, clears the second entity's X velocity, and falls into the attack updater.
Both rotation-pattern selections converge here to clear offset $78, the standard X-velocity field of the embedded second entity record, before entering the update-and-spawn state.

This state runs the shared SniperHoneyviper motion pipeline, attempts an oscillating-shot spawn, and then waits for rotation state two, the delay, and a bounce before selecting the next travel direction.

The block obtains the player delta and selects one of two signed second-entity X velocities, main states, movement modes, and direction-bit values from that sign and SniperHoneyviper's camera-relative X.
Incomplete rotation, delay, and bounce prerequisites converge at this return from the attack update state.
This alternative selects main state $10, movement mode four, positive second-entity X velocity $18000, and a clear direction bit.

Both travel branches call this helper on a screen-X or timer limit; it returns to attack-selection state eight, clears horizontal mode $5C, and derives the next delay from $1E0 minus BossCombatCounter.
The state tests motion phase $16C rather than health. Below six it advances to the refill updater, selects rotation state $A, and clears the second entity's X velocity.

This state contains no fade operation: it runs the motion pipeline, adds four to BossCombatCounter up to $1E0, then waits for the configured delay and a bounce before selecting another travel direction.
An incomplete counter threshold, active delay, or missing bounce returns here without selecting another travel direction.
When either travel branch drives BossCombatCounter negative, this helper enters main state $24, selects horizontal mode eight, and seeds a $40-frame delay; it does not initialize a hover state.
This state adds $1E00 to negative offset $78, the embedded second entity's X velocity, clamps it at zero, and then waits for bounce velocity $54 to become nonnegative before advancing.
Clamped and still-negative secondary-X-velocity paths converge here to test the separate bounce velocity field $54 for state completion.

Boss_SniperHoneyviperBrakeNegativeSecondaryXVelocity adds $1E00 to $78(a5), clamps nonnegative overshoot to zero, and returns here either while bounce word $54(a5) is negative or after advancing state and clearing $78(a5).

In main state $0E, each bounce subtracts $28 from BossCombatCounter and tests the lower camera-relative X bound and delay before either repeating through the negative-velocity braking state or preparing the next attack cycle.
State $0E enters here to consume combat counter and test the lower screen-X bound and delay before repeating or exiting the negative-travel cycle.
The active travel-delay path steps encounter state backward by two and installs negative second-entity X velocity $FFFDA000.
A missing bounce and the repeated negative-travel path share this return.
This state subtracts $2000 from positive offset $78, the embedded second entity's X velocity, clamps it at zero, and then waits for bounce velocity $54 to become nonnegative before advancing.
Clamped and still-positive secondary-X-velocity paths converge here to test the separate bounce velocity field $54 for state completion.

Boss_SniperHoneyviperBrakePositiveSecondaryXVelocity subtracts $2000 from $78(a5), clamps negative overshoot to zero, and returns here either while bounce word $54(a5) is negative or after advancing state and clearing $78(a5).

Each bounce subtracts $28 from BossCombatCounter and tests the upper camera-relative X bound and delay before either repeating through the positive-velocity braking state or preparing the next attack cycle.
A missing bounce and the configured positive-travel repeat path share this return.
The routine performs no descent, position, or velocity comparison. It waits until accumulated movement coordinate $16C falls below six before advancing state.
Both sides of the movement-threshold test return here after the optional state advance.
The active pre-message delay returns here; expiry instead calls BossMessage_Start.
Active message and motion-gate outcomes return here without starting defeat.

The zero-health path sets BossColorEffectFlags to two, clears sprite object flags, enters main state $1E, clears the second entity's X velocity, seeds StageSpawnCountdown to four, and falls into the defeat-motion gate.
This defeat gate selects rotation state $A until rotation reaches $C, then requires a bounce before choosing horizontal mode six, advancing to the defeat sequence, and setting delay $C0.
The already-selected and newly-selected rotation-state-$C paths converge here to test the bounce flag before advancing to the defeat sequence.
All callers are defeat states; the routine applies Gfx_UpdateRandomizedPaletteRange, attempts SniperHoneyviper debris, and tail-runs the shared motion pipeline.

This main-state entry runs the defeat effects while counting down field $5A, applies the full palette fade during the final $1C frames, then clears encounter display state and spawns the alternate transition.
Expiration of the defeat delay enters this block to advance state, clear display controls and unrelated objects, spawn the alternate transition, and apply the completed fade.
This final main-state entry derives a fade parameter while field $5A is at least $30, then counts down $5A and removal delay $4A before setting object flag bit four.
Optional fade-parameter updates converge here before decrementing the fade and removal delays.
The early defeat-sequence fade window and both fade-out countdown paths share this return.
Both active combat callers use this ordered four-stage pipeline: line-scroll positioning, vertical bounce and sprite anchors, horizontal motion, then motion-phase integration and rotation dispatch.
The routine uses field $5C to select one of five relative entries rooted at the bounce-direction handler; it dispatches only the horizontal-motion portion of the boss update.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperDispatchHorizontalMotion indexes these five relative movement handlers with field $5C.
When bounce flag $5E.0 is set, this entry toggles direction bit $5E.1 before selecting horizontal mode A or B; without a bounce it preserves the direction.
Optional direction toggling converges here before flag $5E.1 selects one of the two horizontal motion handlers.
On a bounce this mode seeds horizontal motion field $4C to +$10000, then chooses addition or subtraction of $D000 from the sign of vertical velocity field $54.
The first horizontal mode converges here to select acceleration sign from the high word of vertical velocity field $54.
A negative vertical velocity selects subtraction of the first mode's horizontal acceleration.
On a bounce this mode seeds horizontal motion field $4C to -$10000, then uses the vertical-velocity sign to select the acceleration complementary to mode A.
The second horizontal mode converges here to select acceleration sign from the high word of vertical velocity field $54.
A nonnegative vertical velocity selects subtraction of the second mode's horizontal acceleration.
This shared movement-table return uses the project naming convention without a generated underscore suffix.
This routine adds derivative $178 to motion phase $16C, clamps a negative phase to zero, and dispatches rotation field $174; it is not the boss's complete physics handler.
After clamping the accumulated coordinate, this block dispatches field $174 through the rotation-state table.
Boss_SniperHoneyviperIntegrateMotionPhaseAndDispatchRotation indexes these nine relative rotation handlers with field $174.
This entry advances the rotation state, clears derivative, direction, and timer fields, then falls through into the bounded random-delay angle oscillator.
This is rotation-table state zero; the replacement removes the inconsistent generated underscore.
Both motion-limit outcomes converge here before updating the bounded oscillating angle.
Both rotation-initialization variants enter this shared bounded angle oscillator.
A nonzero direction flag selects angle subtraction and its upper-range reversal tests.
Both oscillator directions and reversal cases converge here to store field $170.
This entry advances the state and clears direction and timer fields before the following phase adds $4000 to the derivative, moves the angle in eight-unit steps, and caps phase $16C at $40.
This is the rotation table's first acceleration state; the replacement removes the inconsistent generated underscore.
Both angle halves converge here to apply a signed eight-unit step and normalize the result.
A zero angle and a completed angle step converge here to clamp the accumulated motion coordinate and optionally advance state.
Limited and still-accelerating paths share this rotation-state return.
The state applies sign- and timer-sensitive four-unit angle steps, accelerates derivative $178, and resets derivative, angle, and timer after phase $16C reaches $40.
A nonnegative motion derivative enters this branch to subtract the four-unit angle step.
Both signed angle paths converge here to accelerate the motion derivative and test its coordinate limit.
Limited and unconstrained paths converge here to store derivative, angle, and timer fields.
This entry advances the state and clears oscillator controls before the following phase accelerates by $6000, reverses at phase $10 with derivative $FFFCC000, and uses random 8-11-unit angle steps.
This is the rotation table's alternate acceleration state; the replacement removes the inconsistent generated underscore.
Both alternate acceleration-limit outcomes converge here before preparing parameters for the shared angle oscillator.

The forward phase targets angle $110 and the reverse phase targets $3A0; completion sets Plane A shake to eight, queues SFX $A1, spawns the circle shot, subtracts $12C from BossCombatCounter, and resets rotation.
The rotation table enters this active spin phase after initialization; the name describes a state rather than preserving an underscore suffix.
Incomplete forward and reverse spin phases share this return.
After the first angle target is reached, this branch rotates in the opposite direction toward the firing transition.
The routine positions the sixteenth entity record from the second, integrates vertical position/velocity with a zero-boundary bounce, and derives jittered and bobbing auxiliary sprite anchors.
Movement-mode-specific constants converge here before vertical position and velocity integration.
Normal integration and the boundary-reset path converge here to store position and velocity fields $54 and $50.
Frame-dependent Y jitter converges here before storing the primary auxiliary sprite position.
Frame-dependent Y adjustment converges here to store the secondary auxiliary sprite X coordinate.
Optional X jitter converges here before storing the remaining secondary position fields.
A nonzero bobbing direction flag selects incrementing the bounded offset toward four.
Both bobbing directions and their bounds converge here to store the offset and derive the linked Y coordinate.

This routine updates two bounded swing angles and direction-frame pointers, derives two endpoints, shifts a five-word rotation history, and positions five consecutive chain-part records with a Y clamp at $144.
Crossing either bound toggles the first swing direction bit before the angle is stored.

Allocation and frame-gate rejections from both adjacent spawners, plus their shared positioning tail, converge on this return.

Every 16 frames, this routine can allocate type $11C, initialize its startup fields and frame, copy a signed frame-source word into horizontal velocity, and use the shared randomized boss-relative positioning tail. Type $11C dispatches to Projectile_MadamBarbarDropUpdate.

The type-$11C dispatch-table entry points here; the routine removes the object when the stage-spawn countdown is active and otherwise updates its startup animation, falling motion, terrain contacts, optional pickup, and explosion conversion.
When StageSpawnCountdown is negative, this block dispatches between state zero's startup sequence and the nonzero falling-motion state.
The startup timer and frame-limit checks return here; after the terminal frame, state is advanced and horizontal velocity is multiplied by eight before the same return.
The nonzero state selects frame $C5, applies $6000 vertical acceleration until the signed threshold, and then probes terrain at the current position.
The block calls Physics_AddEntityOffset with both offsets zero; a nonzero result decrements the contact counter, either restoring upward velocity and frame $D2 or entering the final-contact path.
Negative vertical velocity and a zero terrain-probe result return here, as does each nonfinal contact after upward velocity is restored.
When the contact counter becomes negative, this path makes a one-in-four pickup attempt and, if allocation succeeds, creates a large pickup at the drop object's position with upward velocity.

All final-contact outcomes clear horizontal velocity, write $FFFE into the low word of vertical velocity, and tail-call Projectile_CheckLifetime, which unconditionally converts the current object to the shared type-$C4 explosion form.
Boss_MadamBarbarSpawnAnimationEffect passes this terminated frame script to Sprite_InitFromTable for the type-$38 animation object.

The entity dispatch table selects this routine for Joker's type; it checks initialization fields and shared transition flags, enters the falling sequence when boss health reaches zero, updates palette and screen X when applicable, and dispatches the current state.
The block calls Gfx_ProcessDefaultColorFade and stores camera X plus object X into Joker field $BC before state dispatch.
Initialization bypasses and the normal update path converge here to index a relative-offset table by the state word at object offset four and jump to the resolved handler.
Boss_JokerDispatchState indexes this 20-entry table of signed offsets relative to Boss_JokerInit using the even state word.
State zero advances to state two, clears setup field eight, snapshots camera X into field $48, initializes a four-step counter, and calls Object_ClearAllExceptTypes with limit $15C.
Boss_JokerInit falls through to this return, and Boss_JokerSetup branches here while shared render flag $FFF720 is negative.

State two renders four progressively shifted tilemap steps, then initializes the 19-record metasprite, auxiliary slots, object group, indexed tilemap rows, linked flags, position fields, and initial dive state.
After the setup counter expires, this block marks setup complete and passes Joker-specific descriptor, radius, and link tables with count $12 to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts.
This four-record loop writes object type $10 to slots beginning at $FFCD40 before the root and linked-object initialization continues.
After object and tile initialization, this 18-record loop sets bit seven of byte field three on linked slots beginning at $FFC680.
Boss_JokerSetup passes this 18-byte command stream directly to Tilemap_QueueIndexedRows.

Boss_JokerStretchState reaches this path after its pose completes when field $35C is nonzero and X is below $190; it selects state $18 and resets pose and delay fields. No health check occurs, and the sequence later returns to attack selection rather than defeat flow.
State $18 counts down field $11C, advances to state $1A, and calls BossMessage_Start with selector five while the shared phase-gate pose continues.

State $1A waits while player behavior state $FF80C2 is nonzero; once it clears, the routine advances to state $1C and reloads the delay. The imported defeat-animation description is contradicted by the subsequent return to battle.
State $1C counts down the post-sequence delay, clears shared transition fields when it expires, adjusts two scroll values, and branches back to Boss_JokerSelectNextState.
All three phase-gate states use this block to advance one command stream, adjust body-height field $1DC from pose cursor $58, optionally toggle facing, and render the body.
At pose cursors $10 and four, this path increases field $1DC by two until $56; the renderer uses that field to derive linked-part Y offsets, the boss Y helper, and vertical scaling data.
At other pose cursors, this path decreases body-height field $1DC by one while it remains at least $32.
The body-height paths converge here; when field $3BC is nonzero, pose cursor eight or $14 selects the facing-toggle block before rendering.
At the two selected pose cursors, this block toggles bit $0100 of facing field $54 and copies linked value $370 to $6D0.
All phase-gate pose paths converge here to restore linked anchors $48/$4A, set two Y fields to $144 around Boss_JokerRenderBody, and return.
Boss_JokerUpdatePhaseGatePose is the sole consumer of this looping pose-command stream across states $18, $1A, and $1C.

Boss_JokerMain branches here only after shared boss health $FF8200 reaches zero; the routine sets transition flags, clears object flags, selects state $1E, installs upward velocity and a $80 delay, and enters the falling state.
State $20 applies an increasing fade counter until $20, continues the defeat fall while below the limit, then clears the boss object range and initializes the player-spawn object.
State $1E counts down the $80 delay, advances to fade-out state $20 on expiry, updates the palette fade, and continues the health-zero falling sequence every frame.
Both delay outcomes converge here to call Gfx_UpdateRandomizedPaletteRange before the defeat-fall update.

The delay state falls through and the active fade-out state branches here to spawn a defeat effect, publish shared effect value four, add $3000 vertical acceleration, adjust body height, and render the falling pose.
Once vertical velocity becomes nonnegative, this block reduces body-height field $1DC toward $34 and clamps object Y to $120 while restoring upward velocity at the clamp.
After body-height adjustment, this block compares object Y with $120 and clamps both Y and vertical velocity when the boundary is reached.
All health-zero fall paths converge here to pass the dedicated looping pose stream to Boss_JokerUpdatePose and tail-call Boss_JokerRenderBody.

State $22 subtracts two from the fade counter each frame, advances to cleanup and sets a $70 delay when it reaches zero, then applies the resulting level. This is the inverse of the preceding fade-out, not merely fade completion.
Both active and completed fade-in paths reach this branch to apply half of counter field $A through the shared Joker fade helper.
State $24 counts down the final $70 delay, marks the Joker object for removal, and clears three shared transition bytes when the delay expires.
The active cleanup-delay path and completed shared-field cleanup converge on this return.

The health-zero fall calls this routine every frame. It updates randomized explosion sound, allocates an effect slot, chooses the debris initializer for one random value out of eight and otherwise creates a type-$160 effect, then assigns randomized boss-relative position.
Seven random selector outcomes initialize type $160, set field-three bit seven, derive horizontal velocity from the frame source, and select one of two mapping and vertical-velocity combinations.
Both the debris and type-$160 initialization branches converge here to clear priority byte $20 and place the effect at randomized X and Y offsets around Joker.
Allocation failure and completed randomized positioning share this return.
The Joker fade-out and fade-in states call this local helper, which shifts counter field $A right once and tail-calls Gfx_ApplyFullActivePaletteFade.
Boss_JokerAnimateDefeatFall is the sole consumer of this two-target looping pose-command stream during the health-zero fall and fade-out states.

The routine resets common pose and motion fields, chooses interrupt-wait when shared progress $FF8234 is nonpositive, and otherwise combines absolute player-X distance with frame-derived bits to choose dive preparation or jump preparation. It does not read boss health.
When absolute player-X distance is at least $6A, this block uses the low four frame-source bits to choose jump preparation for value zero and dive preparation otherwise.

The shared-progress selector reaches this path for nonpositive values; it writes state $26 and delay $30 before falling into the interrupt-wait handler. No static evidence identifies the pose as a taunt.
State $26 consumes bit zero of shared byte $FF8260 and returns to next-state selection when set; otherwise it increments shared progress and advances a dedicated looping pose stream.
Setup and next-state selection call this initializer, which writes collision field $26, selects state six, resets pose fields, and installs anchors consumed immediately by Boss_JokerDivePrep.

State six advances the shared dive-and-landing pose until cursor $58 becomes negative, then initializes state eight, body-height acceleration, upward velocity, sounds, and one of two horizontal-motion paths.

After the preparation pose completes, this block plays SFX $44, selects state eight, resets the pose, installs body-height acceleration $FFFEC000 and vertical velocity $FFFB0000, and selects horizontal motion from field $35C.
Field $35C selects fixed horizontal velocity $FFFEC000 when nonzero or the player-directed velocity calculation when zero.
This path obtains signed player-X delta in D1, constructs a positive fixed-point magnitude from high word one and a frame-source low word, and negates it when the player is left of Joker.
Both signed player-directed outcomes converge here to store D0 as horizontal velocity and fall through into state-eight motion.

State eight updates the body-height accumulator and vertical velocity, advances to state $0A when the resulting vertical velocity becomes nonnegative, and otherwise advances its dedicated pose before rendering.
The helper adds $A00 to accumulator $23C, adds that accumulator to fixed-point body height $1DC, and adds $2000 to vertical velocity $1C. It performs no explicit rotation.
When state-eight vertical velocity becomes nonnegative, this block advances to state $0A and resets the pose cursor and timer for the descent phase.

State $0A continues the same accelerated body and vertical motion until linked Y field $374 reaches $144, using a pose stream shared with the later bounce state. No explicit spin operation is present.
Dive descent and the later ground-bounce state converge here to select state $0C, reset pose and anchor fields, clear vertical velocity, play SFX $53, and call Boss_JokerSpawnDescendingShotEmitter.
Boss_JokerInterruptWaitState is the sole consumer of this two-target looping pose-command stream.

Boss_JokerDivePrep and Boss_JokerJumpPreparationState both consume this two-target stop-terminated pose-command stream; the interim landing description was contradicted by the upward velocity installed at preparation completion.
Boss_JokerDiveMotionState is the sole consumer of this two-target stop-terminated pose-command stream.
Boss_JokerDiveDescentState and Boss_JokerBounceMotionState consume this two-target stop-terminated pose-command stream.

State $0C adjusts body-height field $1DC in opposite directions across pose-cursor ranges, slows horizontal velocity, advances a dedicated pose, and selects the next battle or phase-gate state when the pose completes.
For pose cursors below $0C, this block subtracts two from body height while it remains at least $30.
Both body-height directions converge here to slow horizontal velocity, advance the dedicated stretch pose stream, and render the body.
When the stretch pose cursor becomes negative, field $35C and Joker X choose next-state selection, dive preparation, or the phase gate.
The zero-$35C post-stretch path tail-branches to Boss_JokerSelectNextState.
Two next-state selector outcomes call this initializer, which selects state $0E and resets pose and anchor fields for the jump preparation handler.

State $0E reduces fixed-point body height while advancing the pose shared with dive preparation; on completion it initializes state $10 with vertical velocity $FFF80000, proving an upward launch rather than a landing.

After the jump-preparation pose completes, this block plays SFX $44, changes collision field $26, selects state $10, installs vertical velocity $FFF80000, reduces shared progress, and publishes effect value two.

State $10 adds $2000 to vertical velocity, increases body height, and compares the body-derived lower edge with Y $C8 while advancing a dedicated pose; the initial negative velocity makes this an ascent path.

When the body-derived edge moves above Y $C8, this block selects state $12, resets pose, installs accumulator $FFFE0000, clears vertical velocity, emits shared effect value five and SFX $A1, and restores collision field $16.

State $12 adds $1000 toward zero in the negative accumulator and applies that value to fixed-point body height while negative, then derives Y from body height and advances its pose. No falling velocity is applied.
Accumulator outcomes converge here to derive object Y from body height, advance the compression pose, or initialize recovery when the pose cursor becomes negative.
After the compression pose completes, this block selects state $14, resets pose fields, and clears the body-height accumulator before falling into recovery.
State $14 applies an increasing positive accumulator to body height until it reaches $40, deriving Y and advancing a dedicated recovery pose while below the threshold.
The recovery and bounce-motion states call this helper, which adds $180 to accumulator $23C and adds the resulting fixed-point value to body height $1DC; it performs no terrain query.
When recovered body height reaches $40, this block advances from state $14 to state $16 and resets the pose cursor and timer.

State $16 increases the body-height accumulator, applies vertical acceleration, advances a pose shared with dive descent, and enters stretch when linked Y field $374 reaches $140. No attack-specific operation is present.
Boss_JokerJumpAscentState is the sole consumer of this single-target stop-terminated pose-command stream.
Boss_JokerBodyHeightCompressionState is the sole consumer of this two-target stop-terminated pose-command stream.
Boss_JokerBodyHeightRecoveryState is the sole consumer of this single-target stop-terminated pose-command stream.
Boss_JokerUpdateStretchPose is the sole consumer of this four-target stop-terminated pose-command stream.

Every active Joker state reaches this routine after pose or motion updates; it positions 22 linked metasprite records, builds raster work values, writes tile words, and queues two display command blocks.
After optional pointer-pair exchange selected by field $54, this block assigns symmetric X offsets and body-height-derived Y offsets to four linked records before traversing 22 metasprite parts.
Joker X values below $60 or at least $1E0 select this block, which writes the fixed word $FE72 to $FFA908.
For Joker X in the interval [$60,$1E0), this block writes $C0 minus object X to $FFA908.
Both horizontal-offset paths converge here to seed D0 with $80 and prepare a 96-word loop at $FF9520.
This 96-iteration loop writes one word and subtracts two before the next write, producing the descending ramp at $FF9520.
This block derives a RAM center address from Joker Y, seeds both sides with $1B0 minus Y, and prepares 31 paired writes using a step derived from body height.
The 31-iteration loop writes equal starting values outward on both sides of a Y-derived RAM address, adding the body-height step on one side and subtracting it on the other.
After field $29E toggles every 16 frames, this block updates index $29C only on alternating frames and selects decreasing or increasing movement from that toggle.
The increasing half of the oscillation adds four to index $29C and clamps values reaching $10 back to the last valid table offset $0C.
All index-update paths converge here to store $29C and copy four selected words, plus $800-adjusted counterparts, from the secondary table into the two $FF9600 work records.
Boss_JokerRenderBody indexes this 32-word table with frame-counter bits two through four and copies paired words from each 16-word half into two display work records.
The bounded four-value index in field $29C selects paired words from each eight-word half of this table for the same two display work records.
The helper computes (($1DC - $40) / 2) + $C8 and stores it as object Y; contrary to the imported comment, it has no horizontal input.
The helper moves signed horizontal velocity field $18 toward zero by $2000 without crossing through zero.
Positive and negative deceleration paths converge here when their $2000 step reaches or crosses zero.
The non-crossing positive path and the zero clamp converge here to store D0 in horizontal velocity field $18.
An already-zero velocity and the positive or clamped store path share this return.
Negative horizontal velocity adds $2000, clamps to zero if the result becomes nonnegative, and otherwise stores the still-negative result.

All callers supply a state-specific command stream in A1; the routine handles optional SFX, stop and loop controls, resolves a target offset, interpolates ten channels, and publishes linked-part angles.
This block indexes the A1 command stream by cursor $58, handles an optional $80 SFX prefix, and advances to the pose control word.
Both prefixed and ordinary commands converge here to read the control word and test stop marker $FFFE.
After excluding $FFFE, this block treats $FFFF as a loop command that resets cursor $58 and target counter $35E before reading from the stream start.
An ordinary command supplies a low-byte duration and a signed offset into Boss_JokerPoseTargets; the block calculates deltas, installs the duration, and advances the stream cursor by four bytes.
While duration field $C is nonnegative, this block decrements it and applies one interpolation step to ten channels in the $FF9400 work buffer.
All active, stopped, and completed command paths converge here to convert the ten fixed-point channels into angle fields across Joker's linked records.
The pose interpreter calls this helper with a selected target in A0; it supplies Joker's neutral pose, the $FF9400 work buffer, duration, and a ten-channel count to Anim_CalculatePoseChannelDeltas.

This wrapper supplies the $FF9400 work buffer and ten-channel count to Anim_InitializePoseChannelsFromBytes, whose implementation converts source bytes from A0 into initial fixed-point channel values rather than loading timing data.
Boss_JokerUpdatePose adds each command's signed target offset to this base before calculating ten-channel interpolation deltas.

The shared dive and bounce transition calls this routine only when field $35C is zero; it reduces shared progress by $14 and initializes type $198 below Joker with a shot timer of $C0 and emission count four. No static evidence establishes a bomb visual identity.
The field-$35C rejection, allocation failure, and completed type-$198 initialization share this return.

Type $198 indexes this handler directly; while encounter control is active it descends while tracking player X, emits several aimed projectiles on timers, and then converts itself through the shared four-way burst helper.
A negative encounter-control word reaches this active update; a nonnegative value instead marks field-two bit four and returns.
A negative field $24 or exhausted emission count tail-calls Enemy_SpawnQuadProjectiles from this branch.
Until object Y reaches $148, this block adds two to Y and copies the player object's X word at $FFC630 into the emitter X field.
This block decrements timer $48; expiry attempts one aimed-projectile allocation and resets the timer to a frame-derived value from $50 through $CF.
Both successful and failed aimed-projectile allocation paths decrement emission counter $4A here and start the terminal four-way burst when it becomes negative.
An active nonterminal emission and all pre-shot display-field outcomes share this return.
While timer $48 is below $30, this block alternates the high byte of display field $A between $F7 and $F9 from frame-source bit one; otherwise it restores $F8.
Entity type $19C indexes this entry; it updates a palette-fade controller, applies health thresholds, branches to the health-zero transition, publishes screen X, and dispatches the current state.
The state-nonzero paths converge here to call Gfx_UpdateBossPaletteColorFade with color table $3E12 before health and state processing.
When fade-control field $23C is zero, this block selects health threshold $2580 or $3880 from the difficulty flag before comparison.
This block compares shared boss health with the selected difficulty threshold, then distinguishes values below $2380 from the higher threshold range.
The health range at or above $2380 but not above the selected threshold writes the literal value two to shared word $FF8246; no stronger purpose is asserted.
All health-threshold and fade paths converge here to test shared boss health and enter Boss_FlyingNeoDefeatInit only when it is zero.
This block adds plane-position word $FFA900 to boss-relative X field $430, stores the result in linked field $BC, and falls into state dispatch.
The routine indexes a 20-entry relative-offset table with even state field four and jumps to the selected handler relative to Boss_FlyingNeoInit.
Boss_FlyingNeoStateDispatch is the sole indexed consumer of these 20 handler offsets.
State zero advances the state, clears all objects except type $154, builds a sine/cosine table, clears palette high bits, and installs scrolling-background control fields.
Initialization falls through to this return, which is also used while the following scrolling-background wait remains incomplete.
The helper applies mask $7FFF to every word in four palette-buffer ranges; it clears only bit 15 rather than clearing the palette entries.
This loop masks 240 words beginning at $FF4020 with $7FFF.
This loop masks 16 words beginning at $FF4AC0 with $7FFF.
This loop masks 48 words beginning at $FF4360 with $7FFF.
This loop masks 48 words beginning at $FF4400 with $7FFF.
State two calls Tilemap_QueueNextScrollingRow each frame, remains in state while its result is nonnegative, then advances state and clears GlobalSpritePriorityBit.
State four initializes a nine-part metasprite, six auxiliary objects, an object group and palette state, then selects state six with an $80-frame delay and initial position and motion fields.
State six counts down field $1DE while running the common motion, pose, and render path; expiry advances to the next state and calls BossMessage_Start with value seven.
The intro delay, player-sequence wait, and attack-start delay share this path, which updates motion AI, advances a fixed pose stream, and tail-calls the sprite update.
When the intro timer expires, this block advances from state six to state eight and calls BossMessage_Start; it does not initialize an attack.
State eight remains on the common intro-pose path while player-sequence word $FF80C2 is nonzero; when it clears, the state advances and initializes a $30-frame delay.
State $0A counts down the $30-frame delay while maintaining the common intro pose, then tail-branches to Boss_FlyingNeoInitAttackPattern.
The zero-health main path selects state $0C, initializes the first linked-slot cursor and timer, clears motion, sets transition flags, clears object flags, and writes encounter-control value four.
State $0C updates fade, defeat origin, and scroll, then every six frames converts the linked record selected by $4A and advances that cursor by $60 until $C9E0.
Each forward-cursor iteration reaches this block with the pre-increment record in A0 and converts it to an upward-moving defeat particle.
The active six-frame delay and completed forward-slot conversion share this return.
Defeat initialization calls this helper, which sets bit zero in field two of 19 records starting at $FFC680 and separated by the object stride $60.
This 19-iteration loop sets bit zero in the current record's field two and advances to the next $60-byte record.

Both linked-slot walks pass an existing record in A0; the helper reinitializes that record from Projectile_SpawnSpriteFrames as type $38, clears horizontal velocity, installs upward velocity $FFFEE000, and plays SFX $BC.
Only the four defeat states call this helper; it derives fields $70/$74 from boss X/Y with facing-selected X offset $0E or $10 and fixed Y offset $1C, so no collision role is asserted.
Both facing-selected X offsets converge here before boss coordinates are added and the resulting origin is stored in fields $70/$74.
State $0E updates fade, defeat origin, and scroll, then every five frames converts the record selected by $4A and decrements that cursor by $60 until $C9E0.
Each reverse-cursor iteration reaches this block with the pre-decrement record in A0 and converts it to an upward-moving defeat particle.
The active five-frame delay and completed reverse-slot conversion share this return.

State $10 waits on field $48 while updating fade, defeat origin, and scroll; expiry advances state, queues a scroll write, and configures record $FFC9E0 for a facing-dependent horizontal type-$88 launch.
The two facing-selected horizontal velocity signs converge here to tail-call Projectile_InitType88 for record $FFC9E0.
The active state-$10 delay returns here before the fixed type-$88 part is launched.
State $12 updates fade, defeat origin, and scroll, attempts a randomized type-$88 particle every four frames, and after its $70-frame timer advances state and loads a final compressed-tile command.
Facing-selected X adjustment converges here before randomized offsets are added to boss X/Y and stored on the new type-$88 particle.
Frame-gate rejection, allocation failure, and completed particle creation converge here to count down the state timer and perform the final state, timer, field-$62, and tile-command setup on expiry.
The active defeat-particle-rain timer returns here.
State $14 counts down field $48 while updating scroll; expiry advances state, increments $FFA950, and writes player-sequence value $5C.
The active completion delay and the following state-$16 table entry both tail-branch to Boss_FlyingNeoUpdateScroll.
State $18 clears motion each frame, consumes directional bits zero through three of input word $FFF706 to set signed X/Y motion and facing, then advances the common pose and renderer.
After optional bit-zero upward motion, this block tests input bit one and installs positive vertical motion and pose offset when set.
After vertical input handling, this block tests input bit three and installs positive horizontal motion and facing value $100 when set.
After right-input handling, this block tests input bit two and installs negative horizontal motion and facing value zero when set.
All directional-input paths converge here to process the common pose stream and tail-call the sprite update.
The helper selects state $1A, clears the vertical-mode and reversal fields, installs a randomized $40-$43F lifetime, and falls through to restore neutral part anchors.
This shared block points both part-link fields at the boss record and assigns word_EBC18 to both part-mapping fields; it does not allocate any slots.

State $1A counts down its lifetime, oscillates vertically, obtains the player's deltas from the tracked part, updates horizontal pursuit or reversal motion, and renders the pursuit pose while the state remains active.
The active state-$1A path processes pose stream word_3D00A and tail-calls the common sprite update.

The routine uses the signed player-X delta and facing field to accelerate toward the player, terminates pursuit after crossing the player, and reverses horizontal acceleration while field $1DC is active.
The rightward pursuit path reaches this block after applying or capping positive horizontal acceleration, then evaluates the close-range maneuver selector.
With nonzero facing and an active reversal, this path counts down field $11C and applies leftward acceleration until its lower velocity bound.
Both facing-specific reversal paths clear field $1DC here when their $11C countdown expires.
The rightward pursuit reversal subtracts $4200 from horizontal velocity until the value passes $FFFC2000.
The capped and newly accelerated rightward-pursuit reversal paths share this return.
With facing field zero, this path pursues a player to the left, ends the state after crossing the player, or updates the active opposite-direction reversal.
After applying or capping negative horizontal acceleration, this path applies the leftward-side distance gate before calling the common close-range maneuver selector.
The rejected and completed leftward close-range checks share this return.
With facing field zero and an active reversal, this path counts down field $11C and applies rightward acceleration until its upper velocity bound.
The capped and newly accelerated leftward-pursuit reversal paths share this return.
When the adjusted horizontal distance is below $D4, this routine uses frame-counter bits either to arm a three-to-eighteen-frame reversal or to enter the rising-retreat state.
This branch makes reversal field $1DC nonzero and installs a randomized three-to-eighteen-frame countdown in field $11C.
Distances at or above $D4 return here without selecting a maneuver; pursuit-reversal setup also falls through to it.
The helper alternates field $17E between zero and two, accelerates vertically within the $B0-$DC bands, and permits random direction changes near the central $C6 boundary.
This path clears the vertical-mode field and selects upward acceleration unless the upper boundary or central-band random gate switches to downward motion.
This path subtracts $1E00 from vertical velocity while it has not passed the $FFFEE000 upward bound.
The capped upward and downward acceleration paths share this return.
This path sets vertical-mode field $17E to two and selects downward acceleration unless the lower boundary or central-band random gate switches to upward motion.
This path adds $1E00 to vertical velocity while it remains below the $12000 downward bound.
The routine selects state $1C, restores neutral self-anchored part mappings, and resets pose-interpreter fields; contrary to its earlier name, it does not clear either velocity.
State $1C accelerates upward and toward the facing-side screen-X boundary, processes pose stream word_3D01C while in transit, and enters the hover-decision state at the boundary.
The nonzero-facing path accelerates horizontal velocity positively until screen X reaches $1120 or velocity reaches $56000.
Both directional state-$1C motion paths converge here to process pose stream word_3D01C and tail-call the common sprite update.
After crossing either screen-X boundary, this block selects state $1E, fixes Y at $C0, clears motion, installs a $20-$5F decision timer, and chooses facing from screen X.
Both screen-X-selected facing values converge here before the linked-part direction flags are updated.
State $1E counts down field $1DE while rendering the neutral pose, then uses random bit zero to choose either pursuit state $1A or linked-part-anchor state $26.
While the state-$1E decision timer remains active, this path processes pose stream word_3D00A and tail-calls the common sprite update.

The close-range selector reaches this block to choose state $20, install upward velocity $FFFD0000, and reset pose fields before the following handler moves horizontally opposite the pursuit direction until Y is below $A0.
State $20 rises until Y is below $A0, sets horizontal velocity opposite the pursuit-facing direction, renders pose stream word_3D054, and then advances into the diving arc.
The nonzero-facing retreat path stores the exact horizontal velocity $FFFDE000 here before rendering; the preceding compare and add do not alter that final value.
The zero-facing retreat path approaches a positive horizontal velocity and then stores the exact value $22000.
The zero-facing retreat path stores the exact positive horizontal velocity $22000 here before rendering.
Both directional retreat paths converge here to process pose stream word_3D054, update the boss sprites, and assign mapping word_EBBCA to field $3C8.
After rising above Y $A0, this block advances from state $20 to $22, resets pose and horizontal motion, and selects the signed horizontal acceleration word from facing.
State $22 adds the facing-selected horizontal step, accelerates downward up to $40000, periodically plays SFX $D1, and advances to state $24 after reaching Y $D8.
The capped and newly accelerated downward paths converge here before an eight-frame gate optionally plays SFX $D1.
After the optional sound, the diving half of the arc selects pose stream word_3D05E before entering the shared arc renderer.
Both halves of the arc process their selected pose stream, update sprites, and choose the order of mapping pointers word_EBC0C and word_EBC18 from pose field six.
The pose-field-selected mapping order converges here before the two pointers are stored in part-mapping fields $1E8 and $368.
At Y $D8 the code advances from state $22 to $24 and doubles the signed horizontal step used by the second half of the arc.
State $24 subtracts vertical acceleration until rising above Y $B8, applies the opposite signed horizontal step, renders pose stream word_3D070, and then returns to pursuit state $1A.
While Y remains at or below the state-$24 completion boundary, this path subtracts the doubled signed step from horizontal velocity and accelerates vertically upward toward $FFFD8000.
The capped and newly accelerated rising paths converge here to select pose stream word_3D070 and enter the shared arc renderer.
The even decision branch selects state $26, clears pose fields and both velocities, and falls through to the linked-part-anchor handler.
State $26 binds fields $48/$4A to one of the metasprite part records at $FFC800 or $FFC980, updates their mappings from Y, and launches into state $1C at facing-specific screen-X boundaries.
At the facing-selected screen-X boundary this block installs positive vertical velocity and facing-selected horizontal velocity, then enters the horizontal-swoop state.
The nonzero-facing state-$26 path compares screen X with $1000 before either launching or continuing part-anchor updates.
The continuing state-$26 path selects between metasprite part records $FFC800 and $FFC980, exchanging them when pose field six is at least five.

The standalone helper adds four to sp and returns, but no static branch, call, table entry, or envelope-command dispatch reaches it.

Overridden channels, the first DAC record, completed mailbox writes, and FM writes return through this RTS.

These 20 operator register addresses pair with the non-total-level parameter bytes in each 25-byte FM instrument record.

Command 0xF0 enables channel vibrato and stores its parameter pointer, initial delay, step delay, signed delta, half-cycle length, and accumulator state.
Command 0xF1 consumes separate PSG and FM envelope IDs, placing the type-appropriate value in field 0x0A used by the pitch-envelope interpreter.
Command 0xF2 deactivates the current track, silences its FM or PSG output, restores any displaced BGM record, and unwinds the sequence parser.
Negative PSG channel selectors reach this path to issue the PSG mute operation before common stopped-channel handling.
FM and PSG stop paths converge here to test the SFX-processing mode and restore an underlying BGM channel only for an SFX track.
Ordinary FM selectors are normalized here and mapped through the BGM channel-record pointer table after a stopped SFX track.
Ordinary and dedicated FM paths converge here to clear the BGM override flag, mark refresh pending, and reprogram its saved instrument.
After optional FM restoration this path checks whether stopped channel type 2 must clear YM2612 special-mode register 0x27.
Stopped PSG SFX tracks enter here to select either the dedicated PSG override record or the ordinary BGM record for their channel selector.
Non-dedicated PSG selectors are shifted into the BGM channel-record pointer table index at this path.
The selected BGM PSG record has its override bit cleared and refresh bit set, with saved noise control restored for selector 0xE0.
All stop paths discard the dispatcher and parser return addresses here so command 0xF2 exits the current channel update immediately.
Command 0xF3 changes the channel selector to PSG noise, stores its control byte, and writes that byte unless an SFX override suppresses output.
Overridden and successfully written PSG-noise command paths return through this RTS.
Command 0xF4 stores an envelope ID in field 0x0A, whose low bits index Sound_PitchEnvelopePointerTable and whose values are added to pitch.
Command 0xF5 writes field 0x0B, which the PSG playback path uses exclusively as a one-based index into Sound_PSGVolumeEnvelopePointerTable.
Command 0xF6 reads a big-endian signed displacement and moves the sequence cursor relative to the displacement's second byte.
Command 0xF7 selects one of the channel's loop counters, initializes it from the following byte, and jumps while the decremented count remains nonzero.
Initialized and already-active loop counters converge here for decrement, conditional relative jump, or displacement skip.
Command 0xF8 pushes the current sequence cursor into the channel's descending return stack and then applies the shared relative jump displacement.
Command 0xF9 reloads the sequence cursor from the current channel return-stack slot, advances past the saved call displacement, and pops the slot.
Command 0xFA stores one parameter in channel field 2, which duration decoding uses as the per-channel tick multiplier.
Command 0xFB adds its signed parameter to channel pitch-transpose field 8.
Command 0xFC sets bit 7 of field 0x0A, the exact enable bit tested by Sound_ProcessVibrato before updating custom vibrato state.
Command 0xFD clears field-0x0A bit 7, disabling the custom vibrato update while retaining the low pitch-envelope selection bits.
Command 0xFE decodes four frequency-offset selectors into the active FM3 shadow slots and writes 0x40 to YM2612 mode register 0x27.
BGM and SFX processing modes converge here after selecting the corresponding four-word FM3 operator-offset shadow bank.
Each of four iterations converts a command selector through the offset table and stores one FM3 operator frequency offset.
Command 0xFE indexes these four word values and stores the results as per-operator offsets added by the FM3 frequency writer.
Extended command 0 writes four sequence-supplied SSG-EG values to registers 0x90/0x94/0x98/0x9C and forces each operator attack rate to 0x1F.
This four-operator loop pairs one SSG-EG parameter with its SSG-EG and attack-rate register addresses before advancing to the next operator.
The eight alternating bytes provide each operator's SSG-EG register followed by its attack-rate register in the driver's operator order.
Extended command 1 consumes a pause/resume flag and updates exactly the ten BGM PCM, FM, and PSG records while preserving the caller's current channel pointer.
After separately marking the PCM sequence record paused when active, this block prepares six iterations for the following BGM FM records.
Each iteration advances by one 0x30-byte record, converts an active BGM FM record from bit 7 to paused bit 0, clears panning output, and sends key-off.
Inactive and newly paused FM records converge here before the six-record loop advances to PSG handling.
Each of three iterations advances to a BGM PSG record, converts an active record to paused state, and mutes it unless an SFX override suppresses output.
Inactive and newly paused PSG records converge here before the three-record loop restores the caller's channel pointer.
A zero extended-command parameter enters the resume half, beginning with synchronized DAC state and panning reads before reactivating paused BGM records.
The resume path waits for 68000 ownership of the Z80 bus before reading DAC playback state and its two candidate panning bytes.
A nonzero DAC state selects one of the two Z80 panning bytes and writes it to YM2612 port-1 register B6 before channel-record resume.
After optional DAC panning restoration, a paused bit on the BGM PCM sequence record is converted back to active bit 7.
PCM resume and already-unpaused paths converge here to prepare six BGM FM record iterations.
Each iteration advances by 0x30 bytes, converts a paused FM record back to active, and restores panning when no override or active DAC ownership prevents it.
For channel selector 6, the resume path waits for the Z80 bus and samples DAC activity before deciding whether YM2612 panning may be restored.
Eligible resumed BGM FM records write their saved panning/AMS/FMS byte through the current-channel register B4 API.
Unpaused, overridden, DAC-owned, and panning-restored FM paths converge here before continuing the six-record loop.
Each of three iterations advances to a BGM PSG record and converts paused bit 0 back to active bit 7 without writing a note immediately.
Already-running and newly resumed PSG records converge here before the loop restores the caller's channel pointer.
Extended command 2 copies one multiplier byte to field 2 of the ten consecutive BGM PCM, FM, and PSG records beginning at FFF840.
This ten-iteration loop writes the shared tick multiplier and advances by the exact 0x30-byte channel-record size.
Extended command 3 starts the manual BGM attenuation state and installs its FM/PSG step bytes when no prior request owns the transition state.
An idle transition state is changed to pending value 1 here; zero retained steps cause the command's two attenuation parameters to be consumed and stored.
Preconfigured and newly loaded attenuation-step paths return through this shared RTS.
Extended command 4 changes applied attenuation state 2 to restore-request value 0x80; it neither checks a time-based fade nor computes completion.
Non-applied transition states and the newly queued restore request return through this RTS.
When the duration counter has not expired, this path updates note timeout, PSG volume envelope, vibrato, and any selected pitch envelope; the channel is not idle.
Only PSG channel records call this parser; it dispatches command bytes, decodes PSG notes and rests, and saves their duration and cursor.
This loop reads one sequence byte and redispatches values at or above 0xE0 until a note, rest, or duration event is reached.
Bytes below 0xE0 enter here and are separated into signed note/rest values and nonnegative duration values.
This entry passes the event byte to the common duration calculator and then saves the PSG sequence cursor; it does not decode a note.
The routine normalizes PSG note values, applies transpose, indexes the PSG tone-period table, or marks values below 0x81 as rests.
The below-note path sets the rest flag, stores period 0xFFFF, saves the sequence cursor, and conditionally mutes PSG output.
The routine starts from the channel's saved PSG period, applies pitch effects when eligible, and emits the two-byte PSG frequency command.
Sustained PSG updates enter here and skip the frequency write when no pitch-envelope ID is selected.
Resting and overridden channels return; otherwise the common pitch-effect result is encoded for the selected PSG tone or noise channel.
This entry packs the low four and following six period bits into the two consecutive writes required by the VDP PSG frequency latch.
No-envelope, rest, override, and completed PSG frequency-update paths share this return.
The routine is reached only from PSG playback and interprets channel field 0x0B through the PSG volume-envelope table; it performs no FM operation.
New-note and sustained paths enter here to combine base attenuation with the selected one-based PSG volume-envelope stream.
This loop advances the envelope cursor, reads its next byte, and dispatches values 0x80 through 0x83 as cursor or termination commands.
Noncommand envelope bytes are added to base attenuation and clamped to the PSG maximum value 0x0F.
The routine suppresses rest and override output, handles note-stop hold fields, and writes the PSG channel selector combined with attenuation.
Eligible volume paths converge here to combine channel selector and attenuation and write the result to VDP_PSG.
Absent envelope, resting or overridden channel, hold, and completed volume-write paths return here.
When channel bit four is set, fields 0x12 and 0x13 determine whether the current PSG attenuation may still be written.
Envelope command 0x83 backs up the cursor, sets the rest flag, and enters the override-aware PSG mute path.
Envelope command 0x81 moves the cursor back two bytes so the preceding attenuation value is read again on the next update.
Envelope command 0x82 copies its following byte into the stream cursor and immediately reads from that new position.
Envelope command 0x80 clears the stream cursor and immediately restarts interpretation at entry zero.
The wrapper tests channel override bit two and falls through to the low-level PSG mute only when no live SFX owns the output.
The routine combines the channel selector with maximum attenuation 0x1F and writes it to the PSG port.
Override-suppressed and completed low-level PSG mute paths share this return.
The routine writes 0x9F, 0xBF, 0xDF, and 0xFF to apply maximum attenuation to all four PSG channels.

The live arctangent entry. It resolves the four axis cases first and otherwise splits each quadrant by slope so the smaller component is always the dividend, keeping the division inside one word.
A zero delta in both axes and the positive-X zero-Y case both return angle zero.
Zero X with positive Y returns $4000, a quarter turn in the routine's 16-bit angle range.
Zero X with negative Y returns $C000.
Negative X with zero Y returns $8000.
With X positive the sign of Y selects the first or fourth quadrant, and the exact diagonal is answered directly with $2000.
When Y is the smaller component the table is indexed by the Y over X ratio and added to the quadrant base.
When X is the smaller component the ratio is inverted and the table value is subtracted from $4000 instead, which is how one eighth-turn table covers a whole quadrant.
The negative-Y branch negates Y, answers the exact diagonal with $E000, and then splits by slope like the first quadrant.
The low-slope case subtracts the table value from zero, which wraps into the top of the angle range.
The high-slope case adds the inverted-ratio value to the $C000 base.
With X negative the routine negates X, answers zero Y with $8000, and selects the second or third quadrant from the sign of Y; the exact diagonal is $6000.
The second quadrant mirrors the first about $8000, so its low-slope case subtracts from that base.
The high-slope case of the second quadrant adds the inverted-ratio value to $4000.
The third quadrant negates Y as well, answers the exact diagonal with $A000, and splits by slope.
The low-slope case adds the table value to the $8000 base.
The high-slope case subtracts the inverted-ratio value from $C000, completing the eight symmetric cases.
The preserved eighth-turn arctangent table, included from its extracted binary segment; all eight quadrant paths index this one table.

No caller references this routine and its absolute address does not occur in the ROM, while both live entries in the same module are found by that scan. It selects one of three integer square-root paths by magnitude.
For inputs up to $271 the routine subtracts successive odd numbers, which yields a result of at most 25.
A zero input and the completed small-value path share this return.
Inputs between $272 and $FFFF take the eight-iteration restoring algorithm, giving a byte-wide result.
Each iteration shifts two input bits into the remainder and appends one result bit.
Both the subtracting and the non-subtracting outcomes converge on the loop counter.
Inputs of $10000 and above take fourteen loop iterations followed by two unrolled ones, covering all sixteen result bits.
The word-wide loop is the long-operand form of the byte loop.
The fifteenth result bit is unrolled because its comparison must widen to a long.
The sixteenth bit is unrolled again with both operands long.
Both outcomes of the last bit converge here to return the word result and restore the saved registers.
