MessageTileChunkIndex advances by two over four chunks; after the fourth it subtracts six from state, then writes four tilemap words and queues their VDP transfer.
This path clears attribute bit 15 in D2; when it was set, D0 advances eight bytes to select the second half of MessageScript_TileIndexGroups.
The selected tile-index base plus remaining attributes yields four successive words in VDP staging RAM; a DMA command targets the D3-indexed tilemap VRAM destination.
MessageScript_WriteTilemapChunk indexes these four VRAM destination words with D3 values zero, two, four, and six.
MessageScript_WriteTilemapChunk indexes one of four base tile words; MessageScript_SelectTilemapHalf adds eight byte-offset units when attribute bit 15 selects the alternate four.
The zero-value and expired-timer paths of the unreachable renderer share this return.
The value would drift upward by one pixel every other frame while its timer ran.
The block decodes the low twelve bits through Math_PackedBCDLookup into three digits and takes the sign glyph from bit 4 of the low byte.
The four OAM entries are staged eight pixels apart and appended through the shared sprite writer.
Both dash states call this, and the presence of the special-attack object selects the teleport-dash trail mapping over the ordinary one.
The trail is built from two allocations that take the primary and secondary frame lists in turn.
Both trail objects share this block, which copies the player's position and draw bucket and installs the trail's own flags.
A failed allocation leaves the trail incomplete and returns here.
Entity_UpdateHandlerTable drives the trail objects, which fade by toggling their display flag before the motion is applied.
The visible half of the fade sets the flag the invisible half clears.
Both halves converge to apply the stored velocity and spend the trail's lifetime.
The still-running frames return here.
The helper copies the player's horizontal and vertical flip bits onto an effect object so the trail matches the pose that produced it.
The unflipped case returns here without touching the attribute word.

Weapon_UpdateStateAndAmmoRegen indexes this table with each slot configuration after its regeneration timer expires, then adds two to current ammunition and clamps it to that slot's maximum; no animation frame is changed.

UI_UpdateWeaponSelectionObject uses its masked animation phase to select one of this table's six mapping pointers; WeaponSelect_Initialize also indexes the table while constructing the circular selection-slot objects.

The routine first dispatches WeaponStateIndex, then scans four WeaponSlotConfig words, decrements per-slot regeneration timers, adds two to inactive-slot ammunition, and clamps against WeaponSlotAmmoMax; the old animation claim was false.

Normal weapon states retain WeaponSlotOffset as the slot skipped by regeneration; selection states replace it with eight, which matches none of the four offsets and therefore permits every slot to regenerate.
Each iteration uses the slot configuration to reload an expired timer, adds two to current ammunition, and clamps it to the paired maximum; no sprite or animation field is accessed.
This block advances the configuration pointer and logical slot offset by one word before the four-slot ammunition-regeneration loop repeats.

The shared return terminates both the frame-control early exit and the weapon-state handlers that have no further action; its enclosing routine performs ammunition regeneration rather than slot animation.

WeaponSlotOffset selects the active WeaponSlotConfig word in A1; the path prepares Weapon_DirectionVectorPointerBias in A2, decrements nonnegative WeaponFireCooldown, then reaches state cooldown and dispatch.
This branch skips decrement when WeaponStateCooldown is negative; otherwise it subtracts one before dispatching the current state.
WeaponStateIndex is read as a byte offset into Weapon_StateHandlerOffsets; the signed word offset is added to Weapon_GetStateDisplayIndex before jumping through A0.
WeaponStateIndex directly indexes this ROM table; the entries select the state handler or its display index.
WeaponSlotOffset selects the active WeaponSlotConfig address in A0 while WeaponStateIndex indexes Weapon_StateDisplayIndexTable and returns its word in D0.
WeaponStateIndex directly indexes this ROM table; the entries select the state handler or its display index.
This entry saves the active slot offset, advances WeaponStateIndex, resets runtime weapon parameters, initializes angle and radius, then prepares four slot objects and queues sound $C0.
D7 starts at three; DBF initializes four $60-byte slot objects, taking their mapping pointer from the slot configuration and their angle from WeaponSelect_SlotInitialAngles.
The four words $180, zero, $80, and $100 are read successively by the four-iteration slot-object initialization loop.
WeaponMenuSlotOffset indexes these four target-angle words in both initialization and rotation input; initialization adds $100 modulo $200.
If WeaponMenuAngle differs from the selected target, this path adds WeaponMenuAngularStep and masks to $1F0; only at target does it test new directional input bits.
Pressed-input bit three sets angular step to minus $10, advances WeaponMenuSlotOffset by two modulo eight, and queues sound $A8.
Pressed-input bit two sets angular step to plus $10, subtracts two from WeaponMenuSlotOffset modulo eight, and queues sound $A8.
When neither pressed-input bit three nor bit two is set at the target angle, control returns through this RTS.
After masking PlayerPressedInput to its low nibble, any directional bit queues sound $A8; bits zero, one, three, and two select slot offsets zero, four, two, and six in that priority order.
The no-direction branch, bit-zero selection, and final bit-two-not-set branch converge at this RTS.
After bit zero is clear, bit one selects WeaponMenuSlotOffset four and returns; otherwise it continues to test bit three.
After bits zero and one are clear, bit three selects WeaponMenuSlotOffset two and returns; otherwise it continues to bit two.
After higher-priority directional bits are clear, bit two selects WeaponMenuSlotOffset six; a clear bit returns without changing selection.
The helper clears ten words across WeaponTargetOrFrame, WeaponIconFrameTile, WeaponAnimationDataPtr, both motion parameters, and WeaponModeParameter before returning.

Every update copies WeaponMenuSlotOffset to WeaponSlotOffset; defeat state enters the close path, action-state and script gates can commit weapon state, and the remaining path contracts the menu radius.

A nonzero PlayerScriptStateOffset commits the weapon state; otherwise this path subtracts eight from WeaponMenuRadius and either handles open input below $20 or rotates the menu angle according to facing.
This convergence point adds plus or minus $10 to WeaponMenuAngle based on PlayerSpriteAttributes bit three, masks the result to $1F8, and returns.
Once radius is below $20, this path processes rotation input, clamps WeaponMenuRadius to $20, and branches to close on pressed-input bits $70.
Defeat or pressed-input bits $70 queue sound $A7 and set WeaponStateCooldown to eight here; execution then falls through to Weapon_AdvanceCurrentState without an RTS.
The active WeaponSlotConfig word plus two becomes WeaponStateIndex; twice that value becomes WeaponIconTransferState before transient parameters and object blocks 16 are cleared.
A zero WeaponStateIndex clears WeaponSavedSlotOffset; a signed state of at least $12 restores the saved slot, while smaller nonzero states keep D0 and enter transition finalization directly.
The signed compare against $12 branches to finalization for smaller WeaponStateIndex values and otherwise falls through to restore WeaponSavedSlotOffset.
WeaponSavedSlotOffset is copied to WeaponSlotOffset; the restored slot configuration word plus two is stored in WeaponStateIndex before finalization.
This convergence point doubles D0 into WeaponIconTransferState, clears WeaponStateCooldown, and branches to Sys_ClearObjectBlocks16 without writing WeaponStateIndex.
This helper copies WeaponMenuSlotOffset to active WeaponSlotOffset and returns; WeaponSelect_Update calls it before its state and radius gates.

State $02 selects even values $0E, $0C, $0A, or $08 at slot-word thresholds $708, $3E8, and $320; Weapon_FireProjectile copies the result to object field $5E, which the type-$14 update handler decrements as a lifetime.
This convergence stores the selected even lifetime in WeaponModeParameter and branches to Weapon_UpdateTargetingReticle; the firing path later copies the word to projectile field $5E.

State $04 initializes up to four type-$A0 objects whose field $48 expects type $22C, the spread-projectile update type; it then sets a word flag from the slot $10 threshold and enters Weapon_UpdateTargetingReticle.
A free PlayerEffectObjectPool record receives type $A0, flags $8080, and expected parent type $22C in field $48; the type-$A0 handler copies the matched parent transform.
The continuation advances a0 by $C0 and DBF d7 repeats the four-slot companion initialization before the ammo-threshold flag is set.
Both sides of the slot-word $320 threshold converge at this branch to Weapon_UpdateTargetingReticle; no object initialization occurs here.

State $06 chooses a shift from frame phase and random bit or from slot-word thresholds, scales sine-table components into WeaponYMotionParameter and WeaponXMotionParameter, then stores a direction-vector pointer.
Slot word $10(a1) selects sine-component shift two, three, or four at thresholds $3E8 and $708 before the velocity calculation.
A random sine-table offset supplies paired components; shifting by d3 stores Y motion and X motion with twice StageMotionXDelta added.
For slot values below $7D0, the path subtracts eight from d0 and floors a negative result at zero before direction-vector index scaling.
The clamped value is divided by $FA, shifted left two, masked with $1C, and used to load a direction-vector pointer from (a2,d0.w) into WeaponModeParameter.
The state-$08 table entry reaches this routine; it derives motion data from $10(a1), initializes four indicator records, then selects a target from the lock-on or collision lists.
The path compares d0 with $3E8; values at or above that threshold select index $1C, while lower values continue to the scaled-index calculation.
The path subtracts eight from d0 and clamps a negative result to zero before the motion-index scaling step.
The path divides d0 by $7D, shifts left by two, and masks with $1C before the result indexes a motion-pointer table.
The selected longword at -$C(a2,d0.w) is written to WeaponModeParameter before four effect-pool records are initialized.
Each free pool slot receives type $A0, flags $8080, and expected parent type $6C in field $48; type $6C is the seeking-projectile update handler.
The continuation advances a0 by $C0 and DBF d7 repeats the four-slot type-$A0 companion initialization.
The loop reads pointers from LockOnTargetList and tests bit seven of object field $23, selecting the first flagged entry.
The flagged target address in a0 is stored in WeaponTargetOrFrame; held-controller bit four selects direct reticle append or the scan path.
If TargetListCountMinus1 is negative the path returns; otherwise it loads the first CollisionTargetList pointer and field $24 value as the current candidate.
DBF d7 continues at Weapon_State8CompareNextTargetValue; when the loop is exhausted, the selected pointer in a1 is stored in WeaponTargetOrFrame.
The no-target branch and the completed collision-list scan converge at this RTS.
The next CollisionTargetList pointer is loaded into a2 and its field $24 is compared against d0; equal or negative subtraction returns to the loop, otherwise a2 becomes the selected candidate.
The state-$0A handler reads slot word $10(a1), selects a direction-vector pointer directly or through the a2 table, then writes a FrameCounter-indexed color to palette slot 54.
For slot values below $3E8, the path subtracts eight from d0 and replaces a negative result with zero before index scaling.
The clamped offset is divided by $80, shifted left two, masked with $1C, and used to load a direction-vector pointer from -8(a2,d0.w).
The path computes (FrameCounter times two) masked with six and writes the selected color word to PaletteActiveColor54 and PaletteShadowColor54.
These four Genesis color words are indexed by the frame counter and written to palette slot 54 in both active and shadow buffers; their visual owner is not established.
The state-$0C table entry returns when WeaponAnimationDataPtr is zero and otherwise enters a bounded frame advance before selecting color, tile, art source, and DMA command.
This RTS is reached when WeaponAnimationDataPtr is zero or the stored frame offset has reached $20.
WeaponTargetOrFrame is bounded below $20, increased by two, and masked with $1E; nonzero ShootingMode adds a $20-byte offset to select the second color ramp.

The selected color is written to active and shadow palette slot 54, the frame tile word comes from WeaponAnimationDataPtr+$20, and the art source plus VDP command $94009340 tail-call the icon DMA queue helper.
This table has two consecutive sixteen-word color ramps; ShootingMode selects the second by adding $20 bytes before the frame offset is applied.
Weapon_UpdateCurrentState deliberately anchors a2 at the fifth pointer of the 13-entry window.
State six indexes forward, while states eight and ten use negative biases; every target is a direction-vector table rather than opaque motion data.
This even word directly indexes Weapon_StateHandlerOffsets; values $12 and $14 enter the weapon-selection overlay initializer and updater.
This word is constrained to slot offsets 0, 2, 4, and 6 and selects the same active slot across the WeaponSlotConfig, regeneration-timer, current-ammunition, and maximum-ammunition arrays.
The special-state transition saves and restores this slot offset before recovering the active slot record.
WeaponSelect_Initialize sets this radius to $A0; the open-state update contracts it to $20 before accepting input.
The selection updater compares this angle with WeaponSelect_TargetAngles and advances it by WeaponMenuAngularStep.
The shared updater decrements this word and the selection close path sets it to eight before committing the transition.
Left/right rotation input stores signed steps of $10 here and the overlay angle update consumes them.
Directional input writes one of the four slot offsets here; WeaponSelect_CommitSelectedSlot copies it to WeaponSlotOffset.
The screen initializer calls heading, controller-type lookup, status and control-type rendering, and EXIT rendering, then queues six icon tile transfers from ForceTextLayout destinations minus six.
D7 advances by two from zero through $A; each of six iterations reads a force-text layout word, subtracts six, and queues one weapon-icon tile transfer.
The RTS after the six-transfer loop is also the branch target while vertical scrolling or exit tilemap fill is incomplete.
This entry clears WeaponSlotOffset and four WeaponSlotConfig words, then falls through to WeaponSetup_RefillAmmo for eight $3E8 ammunition words.
This routine writes $03E8 to the eight consecutive WeaponSlotAmmo words, starting at WeaponSlotAmmo0.
The DBF loop stores $03E8 in each of eight consecutive weapon-ammunition words before returning.
The update calls WeaponSetup_UpdateBackgroundEffect, indexes the relative state-handler table with SetupTransitionIndex, adds WeaponSetup_HandleLoadoutState, and jumps through A0.
The seven word offsets target loadout, control input, exit input, exit tilemap fill, control-test text, confirmation, and idle handlers relative to WeaponSetup_HandleLoadoutState.

This loadout state renders setup sprites, updates highlight and vertical scroll, waits while the scroll step reports movement, then refills ammo, handles input, and conditionally renders a force cursor.
WeaponSetupForceIndex indexes six force-cursor X/Y pairs; this path writes one cursor sprite and a $FFFF terminator to SharedSpriteScratch before appending OAM.
WeaponSetupForceIndex values zero through $A index these six X coordinates in the one-sprite force-cursor path.
WeaponSetupForceIndex values zero through $A index these six Y coordinates in the one-sprite force-cursor path.

After rendering setup sprites and finishing vertical scroll, the handler refills ammunition, derives a new ShootingMode from pressed direction bits, handles advance or return input, and renders the options.
When D1 is zero, pressed controller bit three changes it to two before the ShootingMode commit; nonzero D1 skips that input test.
If D1 differs from ShootingMode, this path stores D1 and queues sound $DB before checking page-advance input.
Pressed bit one advances immediately; otherwise the handler masks ControllerPressedState by $E0 and advances only when that result is nonzero.
This path adds two to SetupTransitionIndex, subtracts $10 from WeaponSetupVScrollTarget, queues sound $AD, then renders the shooting-mode options.
Pressed bit four backs out by subtracting two from SetupTransitionIndex, clearing WeaponSetupVScrollTarget, and setting PlayerScriptStateOffset to $12; otherwise it only renders options.
After sprite, highlight, and vertical-scroll updates, this state refills ammo; left input stops at index zero, right input stops at 25, and later branches handle forward and back page input.
D1 at $19 skips increment; otherwise ControllerPressedState bit three increments the controller-layout index by one.
When D1 differs from WeaponSetupControlIndex, this path stores the index and queues sound $DB before checking page navigation.
Pressed bit one or any bit in mask $E0 advances the setup page; otherwise this branch checks return inputs.
This forward path writes highlight $E, advances SetupTransitionIndex by two, subtracts $10 from WeaponSetupVScrollTarget, queues sound $AD, and renders the layout page.
Pressed bit zero or bit four selects the return path; with neither pressed the currently selected controller type is rendered.
This return path writes highlight $E, decreases SetupTransitionIndex by two, clears WeaponSetupVScrollTarget, and renders the controller-layout page.
Exactly 26 longword pointers provide TYPE 1-26 strings; WeaponSetup_RenderSelectedControlType indexes them by four times WeaponSetupControlIndex.
The first 26 bytes map displayed indices 0-25 to ControlLayoutFlags and are scanned by WeaponSetup_FindControlTypeIndex; the last two bytes $11 and zero are outside both active ranges.
The exit input state renders setup sprites and waits for vertical scroll; pressed bits $E0 initialize a constant tilemap-row fill, while bits zero or four navigate back.
Without pressed bits $E0, this path tests pressed bit zero and then bit four; either returns to the preceding setup page, otherwise it renders EXIT.
This return path writes highlight $E, decrements SetupTransitionIndex by two, increases WeaponSetupVScrollTarget by $10, and renders EXIT.

The exit-page state calls Tilemap_QueueNextConstantRow four times; after TilemapRowCountdown becomes negative it advances SetupTransitionIndex and clears PlayerScriptStateOffset and SecondaryCameraYPos.

The state-dispatched routine increments SetupTransitionIndex, clears WeaponSetupCursorOffset, queues eight eight-byte ControlTestTextLayout rows through Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped, then tail-jumps to Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes.

This executable loop advances WeaponSetupCursorOffset by eight through $40, reads each record from WeaponSetup_ControlTestTextLayout, and calls Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped before loading the control-test palette.

This is the eight-record, eight-byte-per-record CONTROL TEST layout: each record holds two words and a text pointer, from WeaponSetup_ControlTestText through the weapon-select, shot, jump, mode-change, teleport, counter, and hovering strings.
This state renders the two-sprite confirm prompt and waits for ControllerPressedState bit seven before entering the fade setup.
Confirmation advances SetupTransitionIndex, sets PaletteFadeMode two, clears its color offset, sets mask $E000, queues sound one, then branches to WeaponSetup_RefillAmmo.
The seventh WeaponSetup_StateHandlerOffsets entry targets this single RTS, so the post-confirmation idle state performs no further work.
Pressed bits $E0 advance the active slot offset by two and can enter the next setup state; bit four can select the previous slot, while directional bits change the force within the slot.
When WeaponSlotOffset is zero or pressed bit four is clear this branch enters force-direction input; otherwise it decrements the slot offset after queuing sound $DE.
This path reads the newly selected WeaponSlotConfig word into WeaponSetupForceIndex, copies the slot offset to WeaponMenuSlotOffset, clears fire cooldown, and advances weapon state.
The current force index splits into row bits $C and column bit two; pressed up, down, right, and left bits adjust those components while D2 counts accepted changes.
When the row component D0 is not eight and pressed bit one is set, this path adds four to the row and one to the accepted-change count.
When column component D1 is zero and pressed bit three is set, this path adds two to the column and one to the accepted-change count.
When column component D1 is nonzero and pressed bit two is set, this path subtracts two and increments the accepted-change count.
This path combines row and column into WeaponSetupForceIndex, stores it in the active slot, queues its icon transfer, and only on a nonzero change count queues sound $DB and advances weapon state.
This shared render path clears WeaponSetupCursorOffset and enters the six-force name loop used after loadout and shooting-mode input.
Each pass chooses text color $E100 only when SetupTransitionIndex is zero and cursor offset equals WeaponSetupForceIndex; it then advances the offset by two until $C.
D1 indexes one of six layout words for text position, then twice D1 indexes the adjacent longword text-pointer list before Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped.
The first six words are force-name text positions and the following six longwords are their string pointers; initialization and the force-name loop both read this layout.
The heading path queues WeaponSetup_HeadingText at tilemap word $6294 with D0 set to $A100.
The routine chooses $8100 or $A100 for the SHOOTING MODE label using SetupTransitionIndex and FrameCounter, then renders that label and the MOVING and FIX labels according to ShootingMode.
This branch sets D0 to $A100 for the SHOOTING MODE label when SetupTransitionIndex is not two or FrameCounter bit one is clear.
This path queues WeaponSetup_ShootingModeText at tilemap word $680E using D0, then resets D0 to $8100 before testing ShootingMode for the MOVING label.
The MOVING label path queues WeaponSetup_MovingModeText at $6830; D0 is $A100 only when ShootingMode is nonzero, otherwise $8100.
The FIX label path queues WeaponSetup_FixedModeText at $6840; D0 is $A100 when ShootingMode is zero, otherwise $8100.
This page selects text color $E100 when SetupTransitionIndex equals two, otherwise falls through to the $8100 label color before rendering STATUS WINDOW.
This entry sets D0 to $8100 for STATUS WINDOW and falls through to queue the status label and the selected controller-type text.
This alternate entry keeps caller-supplied D0 for STATUS WINDOW, queues the label at $680E, then branches to selected controller-type rendering.
This helper scans 26 WeaponSetup_ControlTypeValues bytes for ControlLayoutFlags; a miss leaves D1 at 26 and clears the flag byte before storing that out-of-range index.
Each comparison reads one layout-value byte, increments D1 on a miss, and DBF repeats for 26 entries; equality branches to index storage.
This path stores the low byte of D1 in WeaponSetupControlIndex+1; D1 is 0-25 on a match or 26 after an exhausted scan.
WeaponSetupControlIndex selects a value byte written to ControlLayoutFlags and a four-byte TYPE-text pointer; SetupTransitionIndex two selects highlight color $E100.
With color D0 already chosen, this path sets text position $6830 and tail-jumps to Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped.
This path selects text color $E100 when SetupTransitionIndex is four; otherwise the following label selects $8100 before drawing EXIT.

This executable entry loads WeaponSetup_ExitText into a0, sets text position d4 to $690E, and tail-jumps to Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped; the alternate entry supplies the selected color before joining it.
With the chosen color in D0, this path passes WeaponSetup_ExitText and position $690E to Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped.
This helper compares SecondaryCameraYPos with WeaponSetupVScrollTarget, changing the Y position by four toward the target; its condition codes distinguish equal from moving at return.
When SecondaryCameraYPos is below the target, this path adds four to that Y field and sets D0 to one before returning.
The equal comparison reaches this RTS with zero set; the plus-four path reaches it after MOVEQ one with zero clear, allowing callers to wait on BNE.
Bit three of the low FrameCounter byte gates this renderer; when set it builds three fixed sprite entries, otherwise it returns without appending OAM.
This straight-line path writes three fixed sprites at X $158, $178, and $198 with Y $146, terminates the list, and appends OAM; it contains no loop.
Bit three of the low FrameCounter byte gates the confirm prompt; a clear bit returns, while a set bit builds two fixed sprites.
This straight-line path writes two prompt sprites at X $164 and $184 with Y $146 and tile words $C2DE/$C2E2, terminates the list, and appends OAM.
The routine reads WeaponSetupHighlight as the palette index; when it is zero, VBlankFrameCounter bit zero selects index zero or two, and a nonzero value enters the phase-decrement path.
This branch subtracts two from stored WeaponSetupHighlight but leaves the pre-decrement index in d0 for the following palette writes.
This tail masks d0 with $E, indexes the two eight-word highlight color tables, and writes their words to PaletteActiveColor49 and PaletteActiveColor50.
WeaponSetup_WriteHighlightPaletteColors indexes these eight words with masked even offset d0 and writes the selected word to PaletteActiveColor49.
WeaponSetup_WriteHighlightPaletteColors indexes these eight words with masked even offset d0 and writes the selected word to PaletteActiveColor50.
This ten-word data run feeds PaletteActiveColor63 through a phase-derived byte offset; wrap phase $01500000 yields offset $14 and reads the first word of the following color-62 run.
This ten-word run feeds PaletteActiveColor62 through the same phase offset; at wrap phase $01500000 the $14 offset reaches the first code word at WeaponSetup_UpdateBackgroundEffect.
SetupTransitionIndex below $A decreases WeaponSetupBgPhase by $18000 and wraps below $B00000 to $1500000; the other path increases it, then writes palette, raster, pattern, and VDP command data.
This path increases WeaponSetupBgPhase by $18000 and wraps values at or above $1500000 to $B00000 before rendering.
The high word of WeaponSetupBgPhase yields an even byte offset for the two palette reads; this path then seeds raster-line offsets and the background pattern work area.
D7 starts at $60; DBF writes 97 signed words to WeaponSetupRasterLines, starting at one and subtracting two after each write.
Each pass derives two mirrored even indices from the swapped phase accumulator and writes two signed offset words around WeaponSetupOffsetCenter until D0 reaches $600000.
This second offset pass writes two mirrored even-indexed words using a negated plus-two value and a minus-eight value, advancing the accumulator until $600000.
D7 starts at $13; each of 20 iterations writes eight longwords: $EEEEEEEE first, $FFFFFFFF fifth, and zeros in the other six positions.
Phase parity selects low-word pattern bytes $F/$F or $F0/$FF; each iteration writes one dither column, adds full 32-bit D1 with its retained high word, and loops below Z80_RAM.
The even-phase first-band branch sets low words D1=$F0 and D2=$FF before calling the shared seven-byte column writer.
This path calls WeaponSetup_WriteDitherColumn, restores the phase accumulator with SWAP, adds full longword D1, and repeats while below Z80_RAM.
The second band selects low-word patterns $E/$FE or $E0/$EF by phase parity, writes columns until Z80_RAM, then queues the background VDP command.
The even-phase second-band branch sets low words D1=$E0 and D2=$EF before calling the shared seven-byte column writer.
After writing a second-band column, this path restores D0 with SWAP, adds full longword D1, loops below Z80_RAM, and finally prepares VRAM destination $7000.
D0 supplies an aligned column offset and a two-bit subindex; this helper derives an address in the shared pattern buffer and writes seven bytes from D1/D2 at offsets four through $1C.
